text: RECENT DOCUMENTS AND THE FOUR ROLES ARE ONE SECTION, AS THE DESIGN DRAWS THEM. They were two full-width sections with four others between them: the documents, and — at the foot of "Find Schemes for You" — a row of four pills reading "For Students", "For Beneficiaries" and so on, offered to a reader who had just been asked which group they belong to, with nothing explaining why. Now the documents take two thirds of the row and beside them sits the brand panel the design draws: "Explore Specific Benefits", the line "Choose your role to discover services made for you", and the four roles DBIM asks a departmental home page to address (§A.4.1 ix) one at a time, in the design system's own Carousel. Nothing is reachable only by rotating it — each of the four pages is in the masthead's Department menu and in the footer. Each document card now carries what the design gives it: the title, what the register publishes about it, and two actions — "View Online" to this site's record of the document, and "Download" to the register's own file, marked as leaving the site because it is served from the Department's CDN. The description the design shows under each title is NOT there: the register publishes none, and a sentence we wrote about a document we have not read is not something a government page may carry. One layout note worth keeping: the grid's single column is `minmax(0, 1fr)` rather than the implicit `auto`, because an auto track takes the largest min-content of its items and the carousel reports the width of all four slides end to end — 944px inside a 343px phone, which cut the documents and the heading off at the right edge.
